subject: Clarify: minute-based vs token-based metering for streaming + rounding floor
content:
From: Emily Zhao <emily@novaplus.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Victor Lin <victor.lin@minuteman.ai>, NovaPlus Accounting <accounting@novaplus.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify billing units for streaming use case

Hi Sergio,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. One follow-up from our engineering and finance teams: our product emits short streaming calls (avg 12s) roughly 8k times per hour, with a heavy tail of occasional longer sessions. Your team mentioned token-based billing with a 100-token rounding quantum and also a "per-minute" option for dedicated customers — it's not clear which applies to streaming/heartbeat traffic.

Two concrete asks:
- Can you confirm how short streaming calls are aggregated for billing (do you round per-call, per-minute, or aggregate across a conversation ID)?
- If we move to a commit with a discount, is there a recommended packaging (e.g., committed tokens vs committed minutes) that reduces the rounding inefficiency for us?

We're trying to model a P&L so a couple of sample invoice calculations would be hugely helpful.

Best,
Emily Zhao
Head of Platform Partnerships
NovaPlus

---
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily@novaplus.com>
Cc: Victor Lin <victor.lin@minuteman.ai>, NovaPlus Accounting <accounting@novaplus.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify billing units for streaming use case

Thanks Emily — great questions. High level: our hosted API defaults to per-token metering with a configurable quantum (100 tokens by default). For Dedicated and Private customers we offer a couple of packaging patterns:

1) Committed tokens (standard): billed per-token, tokens are rounded up to the configured quantum per call by default; we can configure aggregation windows (e.g., 60s) to merge short calls that share a conversation_id for billing purposes.

2) Committed minutes (optional add-on for streaming-heavy workloads): metered by active-connection minutes (one-minute granularity), which avoids token-rounding for many short heartbeats. Pricing for committed minutes is negotiated and typically maps to an equivalent token baseline + an operational premium.

For NovaPlus specifically, given your 12s average calls, minute-based billing reduces rounding waste but requires us to agree on how we detect an "active connection" (continuous heartbeat vs intermittent).

I'll loop in Kimberly to sketch a couple of example invoice calcs and a pros/cons table.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Zhao <emily@novaplus.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, NovaPlus Accounting <accounting@novaplus.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 14:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify billing units for streaming use case

Emily — attaching two quick worked examples (see sheet tabs):
- Scenario A: Committed tokens, 100-token quantum, no aggregation.
- Scenario B: Committed tokens with 60s aggregation window (calls within same convo_id aggregated).
- Scenario C: Committed minutes, 1-minute granularity priced at token-equivalent.

Key assumptions in the workbook: 8,000 calls/hour, avg 12s call duration, avg response payload 80 tokens. I also show the rounding inefficiency percentage for each setup.

Summary bullets:
- If you keep per-call rounding with 100-token quantum, you see ~40-55% token waste depending on payload variance.
- Aggregating by conversation_id with a 60s window reduces waste to ~6-12% for your traffic pattern.
- Committed minutes eliminate token quantum waste for short heartbeats but cost ~5-8% more in equivalent-compute pricing in most cases; it wins when avg-call < 20s and calls are frequent and steady.

We can move the quantum to 50 tokens to reduce waste further but that increases metering overhead and slightly increases metering cost on our side (we normally reserve that for larger commits).

Attachment: redwood_pricing_scenarios_NovaPlus_v2.xlsx (xlsx)

Let us know which scenario you want modeled into a proposed MAP and I'll draft numbers including discount tiers.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Pricing & Packaging, Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily@novaplus.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: NovaPlus Accounting <accounting@novaplus.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify billing units for streaming use case

Quick follow up with concession framing and next steps.

Emily — based on Kimberly's calc, for a 12-month committed deal (NP-7843) with a 30% volume discount at the committed baseline, we can offer: 
- Option 1 (token-commit, 100-token quantum, 60s aggregation): baseline = 1.2B committed tokens/month; effective blended price = $0.0007 per token after discount; expected rounding inefficiency ~7%.
- Option 2 (minute-commit, 1-min granularity): baseline = 18M committed minutes/month; blended price equivalent = $0.00074 per token-equivalent; expected rounding inefficiency ~0% but with a 6% operational premium baked into the price.

Concession notes: the minute-commit includes a 30% SLA credit if we don't meet throughput SLAs in a quarter. Token-commit includes a 15% true-up grace in quarter one for traffic pattern tuning.

Attached is a clean one-page proposal (proposed-MAP-NP-7843.pdf) outlining the options and the mechanics for aggregation windows and heartbeat detection logic. If NovaPlus prefers, we can pilot minute-commit for 2 months with auto-opt-out if usage diverges from projections.

Next steps:
1) Tell us which option you prefer to put into a draft DocuSign (we'll include the minute-detection appendix if Option 2).
2) If marketing/finance wants specific invoice examples for the first three months under Option 2 pilot, call out target months and we'll produce sample invoices.

Thanks — I'll set a 30-min follow-up for tomorrow if that helps.

— Tessa Morgan
Head of Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-MAP-NP-7843.pdf (pdf)
